title: claude v3 contract is zero-tolerance for self-recovered is_error tool completions

evidence.note: run_fault provider_fault at turn 2: 'Claude tool completion differs'. Trigger: a Read of a nonexistent path returned is_error; the turn's stream continues to a terminal result event, so the provider completed the turn after the probe

same fault class, turn 2. Trigger (stdout stream line 13976): a Read of a binary .bin artifact refused by the CLI with is_error ('This tool cannot read binary files'); the stream again reaches a terminal result event afterwards
third attempt completed four turns, adhered, exit 0 - the probing behaviour is per-authoring-session, not deterministic

fourth instance, turn 2, on a different tool: a Grep whose pattern ripgrep rejected ('regex parse error') returned is_error; the stream continues to a terminal result event, so the provider recovered within the turn again. The class is any-tool is_error, not Read-specific
third swiglu attempt completed four turns, adhered, exit 0 - same retry-recovers pattern as softmax: the probing behaviour is per-session luck, and each fatal refusal costs a full campaign's tokens

observation: lab/claude.py:275-279 rejects any tool_result whose is_error is truthy, whose id was never registered, or that repeats a completion - and the check replays the whole captured stream after the CLI exits. Both softmax failures were authoring probes (nonexistent path; binary artifact) that the provider visibly recovered from within the same turn, yet each killed the campaign post hoc. Two campaigns and ~7M provider tokens were spent before a clean third attempt. The swiglu-20260910b recurrence generalizes the trigger beyond Read to any tool: a malformed Grep pattern rejected by ripgrep kills the run the same way.
proposed_change: Route a self-recovered is_error completion to turn-local feedback instead of a campaign-fatal fault: either count it against the turn's protocol adherence report without terminating, or reject only completions that break pairing (unregistered id, duplicate completion) while letting recovered is_error results pass with the fact recorded in ProviderAuxiliaryActivity. This keeps zero tolerance for structural mismatches and stops spending campaigns on probes the provider already survived.
verified_by: Replay: tests/contracts/test_claude_provider.py asserts a turn whose tool completion carries is_error now parses, records the fact as error_recovered exactly once for that invocation, and still normalizes end to end; and that an unregistered id, a repeated completion, a non-boolean flag and an error on the StructuredOutput terminal tool each still raise. The cited campaign streams are not re-processed here, so this verifies the contract, not those two workspaces. Landed in commit d16b1975 on main.
verification_plan: Protocol tick, replay-verified: replay the captured stdout streams from the softmax-20260909b and -c evidence objects through the successor claude.py parser; both must parse to an adhered turn with the probe recorded as auxiliary activity.
